purpose: A bounded, verifiable method for turning a sold medical-alert account into a system that actually works in one particular home: measuring the dwelling's radio, power and connectivity conditions instead of quoting a specification sheet, fitting a device class and a wearable form to the person who must press the button, framing automatic fall detection as the probabilistic supplement it is, building a monitoring-centre account whose dispatch address, entry method, contact tree and response instructions a stranger can act on at three in the morning, proving the whole chain with a mandatory end-to-end signal test that a partial pass fails, training the wearer to demonstrated teach-back, briefing the family on what the service is not, documenting every measurement and every limit found, and deciding at a binary gate whether the account goes live or the visit ends unfinished.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
the operator sells emergency-signaling equipment and resells a monitoring subscription; nobody in the installing role is a licensed clinician and no clinical service is delivered at the visit
the wearer is an older adult treated throughout as a member of a vulnerable-consumer class, and the person paying is frequently not the person wearing the device

reliability properties - radio range, backup runtime, cellular coverage at the bedside, fall-sensor behaviour, voice audibility from the floor - are properties of specific equipment inside a specific building and are established by measurement per installation, never inherited from a brochure

the monitoring centre is a contracted third party whose platform fields and operating protocols bound what can be configured, so what the centre will do is confirmed with the centre rather than promised to the household

licensing, alarm-permit, telecommunications, lockbox and personal-data obligations differ by jurisdiction and change over time; each is named here as an obligation class the operator must verify currently in their own jurisdiction
installations happen both on site and by guided remote setup of a shipped device, and both are held to the same verification requirements
exclusions: customer acquisition and offer economics: the buyer triangle of wearer, adult-child payer and professional referrer, referral-channel building, price and plan design, vulnerable-consumer selling discipline, honest competitive positioning and the decision to sell at all - that is the market and ethical-senior-sales knowledge base this one receives a signed, disclosed account from

running the live subscription after go-live: periodic test-call cadence, battery and device-health monitoring, keeping the address and contact tree current over time, family communication rhythm, service recovery after a missed signal, dignified cancellation when a wearer moves to higher care or dies, and referral loops from well-served families - that is the monitoring, retention and caregiver-relations knowledge base this one hands the live account to

any clinical work: fall-risk assessment, capacity or cognition determination, medication or diagnosis discussion, interpretation of a physician's instructions, or advice on whether an older adult can safely live alone
home-safety modification and general contracting: grab bars, ramps, lighting changes, rug removal, electrical or plumbing work, door hardware and locksmithing

asserting figures as fact - response times, backup-battery hours, radio range in metres, fall-detection percentages, monitoring wholesale rates or subscription prices; every performance property is either measured in this home and recorded with its location and timestamp, or described as a mechanism with its limits and the contractual commitment the operator actually holds

guaranteeing what emergency services will do, how quickly they will arrive, or how they will handle entry; local emergency-service, alarm-permit and lockbox conventions are an obligation class to verify locally rather than assume
personalized financial, legal, tax, insurance or medical advice, including whether any benefit programme or policy will reimburse a monitoring subscription
the monitoring centre's internal operations - staffing, operator training, redundancy and platform engineering - which the operator contracts for and verifies rather than runs

competency_questions.question: Which device class - an in-home base with a worn pendant, a mobile cellular unit with location, or both - fits this household, and what evidence from this home decides it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DEVICE_CLASS_SELECTION states the decision rule keyed to measured coverage and sustainable habit, CONNECTIVITY_PATH_ASSESSMENT and WEARER_FIT_PROFILE supply the findings it cites, and the routine the chosen class does not cover is named

competency_questions.question: How do I assess a home before I commit to a configuration, and which things must I measure rather than assume?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HOME_SITE_SURVEY defines the walk-through and its record, and RANGE_AND_DEADSPOT_TEST defines the worn-pendant walk test with per-location pass, marginal or fail results

competency_questions.question: What may I honestly say about automatic fall detection, and what must I never claim?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FALL_DETECTION_FRAMING gives the mechanism explanation, the supplement-not-substitute sentence and the prohibited claims, CAPABILITY_TRUTH_RULE supplies the measure-before-claim rule, and FALL_DETECTION_VERIFICATION states what can and cannot be verified

competency_questions.question: What happens to this system when the power or the broadband goes down, and how do I verify that rather than repeat the brochure?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: POWER_AND_BACKUP_ASSESSMENT describes outlet selection and the observed unplug behaviour, and CONNECTIVITY_PATH_ASSESSMENT identifies which paths share a failure point with the router

competency_questions.question: How is the monitoring-centre account built so a signal reaches the right address with instructions a dispatcher can act on?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MONITORING_ACCOUNT_SETUP defines device provisioning and the dispatcher-facing record with a verified dispatch address, and RESPONSE_PROTOCOL_CONFIG defines the per-account modifications confirmed with the centre

competency_questions.question: Who goes on the emergency contact tree, in what order, and what must be true of each entry before it is saved?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EMERGENCY_CONTACT_TREE orders by real reachability rather than seniority and requires a live verification dial and consent per entry, with the wearer holding the right to exclude

competency_questions.question: How does a responder get into the home when the wearer is on the floor and cannot open the door?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RESPONDER_ACCESS_PLAN names the entry options, requires the key or code to be tested during the visit, and records the household's own choice between a lockbox and forced entry

competency_questions.question: What exactly does the mandatory end-to-end test consist of, and what result lets me leave the house with the account live?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: END_TO_END_SIGNAL_TEST specifies the hard-location press, the floor-level two-way voice leg, the operator read-back, per-button identification, test flagging and the full repeat after any fix; GO_LIVE_HANDOFF_GATE makes a passed test a binary go-live condition

competency_questions.question: How do I train an older adult so that they actually press the button, including after an embarrassing false alarm?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: WEARER_TRAINING requires the wearer's own demonstrated press from a hard location, when-to-press stated in their own words, cancel practice and the shower and night-wearing habits

competency_questions.question: Where is the line between fitting equipment and giving medical advice when the family asks me care questions in the living room?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NON_CLINICAL_BOUNDARY supplies the redirect, the limits on what may be written into account fields and the referral routes, and INSTALL_SCOPE_CHARTER places clinical work outside the visit

competency_questions.question: What do I do when the wearer does not want the device but the adult child has already paid for it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: WEARER_CONSENT_AT_INSTALL makes wearer assent the condition of installing and defines the recorded-refusal path, and CAREGIVER_ORIENTATION sets what the payer is told

competency_questions.question: How do I run the same protocol when the device is shipped and no technician ever enters the home?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REMOTE_SETUP_PROTOCOL reproduces every mandatory element by guided call, lists what could not be verified, schedules a re-test, and states the stop condition that forces a site visit or a return

competency_questions.question: What documentation must exist when the visit ends, and what is each part of it for?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: INSTALL_DOCUMENTATION_PACKET separates the internal reconstruction record from the large-print household card and states the coverage limits found, and GO_LIVE_HANDOFF_GATE requires an artifact per condition

competency_questions.question: Where do the base unit and the supplementary buttons physically go, and what makes a placement wrong?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MOUNTING_AND_PLACEMENT_PLAN ties siting to the dead-spot map, voice reach from the bathroom floor, an unswitched outlet and the tenancy constraint, and requires a post-placement retest

glossary.definition: The equipment class this business installs: a worn help button that raises a signal to a monitoring centre, usually with two-way voice, in either an in-home form (a mains-powered base station plus a radio-linked pendant) or a mobile form. It is emergency-signaling equipment, not a medical device consultation and not a care service.

A self-contained worn unit with its own cellular radio, speaker and microphone and usually a location function, so it signals from anywhere the carrier reaches. It trades the in-home unit's mains power, loud voice and long battery life for daily charging, weaker outdoor voice and location accuracy that varies with sky view and building mass.

A sensor-and-algorithm feature that infers a fall from an impact-and-stillness signature and raises an alert without a press. It is probabilistic: slow slides, soft landings and falls while the device is off the body may produce nothing, while heavy sitting or a dropped pendant may produce a false alert. It supplements the button and never replaces it.

A location inside or around the dwelling where a worn pendant's press does not reliably reach the base station, produced by construction, distance, body attenuation or interference. Dead spots are found by pressing from real locations with the pendant worn, not by reading a range figure.

The speech path that lets the monitoring operator talk with the wearer after a signal. It is the difference between an alert and a conversation, and it is only proven by speaking from the floor of the far room, at the volume and posture of someone who has fallen, not from beside the base.

The contracted third party whose operators receive signals, attempt voice contact, work the account's instructions and contact tree, and request emergency dispatch. Its platform fields and protocols bound what an installer can configure, so every special instruction is confirmed with the centre rather than promised to the family.

The address responders are actually sent to, complete with unit or apartment number, building name, entry lane and cross street where addressing is ambiguous. It is verified against the premises during the visit and kept distinct from the billing address of an adult-child payer.

The ordered list of people the centre calls around a signal, with each entry's relationship, availability window, keyholder status and verified number. Ordering is by who can actually arrive and answer, not by family seniority, and every entry has agreed to be listed.

The mandatory pre-go-live sequence that proves the whole chain at once: a press from a hard location, floor-level two-way voice, the operator's read-back of the live account record, distinct identification of each button, and the test flagged and logged. A partially passed sequence is a failed test and is repeated in full after the fix.

A fixed, code-opened box holding a door key so responders can enter without forcing the door. It is an entry mechanism with a real security trade-off, chosen by the household rather than by the installer, and its code lives in the monitoring account under the operator's data-handling rule rather than on a note in the home.

nodes.definition: Fix what an installation visit is and is not before the van is loaded. In this business an install is the configuration and physical verification of emergency-signaling equipment plus the creation of a monitoring account a central station can act on: a device class chosen against measured conditions in this dwelling, hardware placed and paired, an account record a stranger can read under time pressure, an end-to-end test that proves a signal travels and a voice is heard, and a wearer who has demonstrated the press. It is not a clinical visit, not a home-safety inspection, not an electrical or plumbing job, and not a second sales call in the living room. The charter also names the stop rules, the conditions under which the technician does not complete the install and leaves the account not live: no wearer assent, no dispatch address verified against the premises, no passed end-to-end test, no reachable consenting contact, or a building whose measured connectivity cannot carry the device class that was sold. Finally it names the two handoffs that bound the work: the disclosed offer and signed agreement arrive from the acquisition side, and a live, documented account leaves to the monitoring side at the go-live gate.

included: the definition of a completed install and its artifacts
the stop rules that end a visit without go-live
the inbound handoff from sales and the outbound handoff to monitoring
excluded: pricing, plan structure and contract terms, which arrive already disclosed from the acquisition side
ongoing monitoring service, test-call cadence and account maintenance after go-live
clinical assessment of any kind
home modification, electrical, plumbing or locksmithing work

pros.claim: A written definition of done turns the word installed from an opinion into a checkable state that survives a busy day
pros.example: two technicians disagreeing about whether a system with an untested bathroom voice leg counts as installed, settled in one line by the charter

pros.claim: Naming the stop rules in advance means the hard decision at 7pm has already been made in the calm of the morning
pros.example: a technician leaving an account not live because no contact could be reached, without needing to invent a policy on the doorstep

cons.claim: A strict definition of done guarantees a proportion of visits end unfinished and cost a second trip the operator absorbs
cons.example: returning to an apartment a week later because the bedside cellular reading would not support the mobile unit the household had bought

cons.claim: A charter written once drifts from what the monitoring centre and the current hardware actually require
cons.example: a condition list that still assumes a landline path after the operator's account base moved to cellular units

failure_modes: treating a powered-on device with a blinking light as an installed system
letting a commitment made during the sale define when the visit is finished
leaving an account live at the centre when a mandatory condition was not met
no written boundary, so installers improvise on clinical and home-modification requests
acceptance_tests: the charter enumerates every condition that must be true for an account to go live, and the technician can point to the artifact that proves each one
a visit that ends without go-live is recorded as incomplete, naming the failed condition and a return date
revisit_triggers: a new device class or monitoring platform is adopted
a delayed or missed signal traces back to something the charter never required
the monitoring centre changes the fields or evidence it requires at account creation

base.update_signal: an incident review or a monitoring-centre complaint shows a go-live condition was missing from the charter, or the operator adopts new hardware or a new centre

nodes.definition: Hold the line between fitting emergency-signaling equipment and practising a clinical trade, because that line gets tested repeatedly and informally inside the home. Families ask, in the hallway and over tea, whether the wearer should still be driving, whether the device will help with dizziness or a new medication, whether it can warn of a stroke, whether it is time for assisted living. The installer answers the equipment half of the question fully and declines the clinical half in the same breath and without embarrassment: what the button does, what the sensor can and cannot detect, and a referral back to the physician, the discharge planner or the home-care agency for anything concerning the person's body, medication or care plan. Practically the boundary shows in what gets written down. The account's information fields carry what the household chooses to state for responders, in their own words, and never a diagnosis, a risk score or a characterization the installer authored. Fall-risk assessment, capacity and cognition determinations, and any judgment about whether the person can safely live alone stay outside the visit entirely. The device is never positioned as preventing, treating or predicting anything.

included: the spoken redirect for clinical questions and the referral routes
what may be written into dispatcher-facing information fields and in whose words
the prohibition on prevention, treatment and prediction language
excluded: fall-risk scoring, capacity or cognition determination, medication and diagnosis discussion
advising whether the wearer can live alone or should move to higher care
interpreting a physician's instructions or a care plan
the household's own decisions about care, which are theirs to make

pros.claim: Declining clinical questions protects the wearer from confident advice by someone unqualified to give it and the operator from a liability class it cannot carry
pros.example: declining to say whether a new blood-pressure medication makes night falls likely, and routing the question to the prescriber the same afternoon

pros.claim: A clean boundary makes the installer more credible on the things they do know, because the refusals are visibly principled rather than evasive
pros.example: a discharge planner who keeps referring because the technician never oversteps into her territory

cons.claim: The redirect reads as unhelpful exactly when the family wants reassurance, and a competitor who answers freely sounds more confident
cons.example: a daughter asking whether this will stop her mother falling and hearing that no device prevents a fall

cons.claim: The line is genuinely blurry in places, and over-refusing can leave a household without practical information they needed
cons.example: refusing to discuss shower use at all when the real answer is simply the device's water rating and where the wall button goes

failure_modes: an installer volunteering a fall-risk or capacity opinion to seem helpful and close the visit
writing a diagnosis or a clinical characterization into the account notes
describing the system as preventing falls or watching over the wearer
answering a medication or care question because the family insists and no one else is there
acceptance_tests: dispatcher-facing information fields contain only household-supplied statements in their own words, with no installer-authored clinical characterization
the visit record shows each clinical question that arose logged with the referral that was given
revisit_triggers: a recurring question type the redirect does not cover appears across visits
the monitoring centre changes which medical or personal fields it accepts
a complaint or referral partner reports that medical advice was given at an install

base.update_signal: a complaint, a referral partner's feedback or an incident review shows an installer crossed into clinical territory, or the centre changes its accepted information fields

nodes.definition: Every reliability claim made about this system must be produced by a test on this equipment in this building, or it is not made at all. The claims that matter are exactly the ones brochures answer generically: how far the pendant reaches, how long the base survives a power cut, whether the cellular path is usable at the bed and in the bathroom rather than at the front window, whether the wearer can be heard from the floor of the far bedroom, whether the fall sensor fires on this person's movement. Each is a property of particular hardware inside a particular structure. The rule has three parts. Measure it, recording the value or the pass, marginal or fail result with the location and the time. Say only what was measured, since a range figure quoted from a specification sheet is not evidence about this house. And write down what could not be verified so that it is never silently assumed. Where a property genuinely cannot be established at an install, such as the centre's answer performance across a year or the sensor's behaviour in a real fall, the honest form is a description of the mechanism, its limits, and the contractual commitment the operator actually holds, never a number invented because it sounds reassuring.

included: the measure-before-claim rule with location and timestamp
recording unverifiable properties explicitly as unverified
expressing untestable properties as mechanisms plus the operator's actual contractual commitments
excluded: repeating manufacturer marketing claims as findings
asserting response times, battery hours, range in metres or detection percentages
any implied medical or preventive performance
the monitoring centre's internal performance engineering

pros.claim: Measured claims survive the first incident review and the first family argument, because the record shows what was tested and exactly where
pros.example: a documented range failure at the back fence that turns a later missed press in the garden into a known, disclosed limit rather than a surprise

pros.claim: The discipline transfers: an operator who measures range and signal also stops quoting response times and detection rates it cannot substantiate
pros.example: sales collateral rewritten to describe the monitoring contract's actual commitment instead of an industry answer-time figure

cons.claim: Measuring consumes visit time and sometimes produces the inconvenient answer that kills the configuration the household preferred
cons.example: a bedside signal reading that rules out the mobile unit the family had already chosen online and paid for

cons.claim: Honest unverified labels make the paperwork look weaker than a competitor's confident specification sheet
cons.example: a record stating that backup duration is manufacturer-stated and unobserved, next to a rival brochure quoting a firm figure

failure_modes: quoting brochure range as though it had been measured
testing only next to the base and recording a single range OK
writing a result with no location and no timestamp
letting a claim survive in the record after firmware or a carrier change invalidated it
acceptance_tests: every reliability statement in the install record traces to a logged measurement with location and timestamp, or is explicitly marked unverified
no figure appears in customer-facing material that cannot be produced from a test log or the monitoring contract
revisit_triggers: a firmware, hardware revision or carrier network change alters measured behaviour
the monitoring contract's commitments change
a real event contradicts a claim recorded at install

base.update_signal: a firmware, hardware or carrier change alters measured behaviour, or an incident shows a recorded claim was never actually tested

nodes.definition: Treat the older adult, not the person who paid, as the one whose agreement makes the installation legitimate, and re-establish that agreement at the door rather than assuming it survived the sales conversation. The visit opens by telling the wearer plainly what is about to be attached to their home and their body, what the monitoring centre can hear and when it can hear it, what a mobile unit's location function does and does not reveal, and which family members will be told about presses or low batteries. Assent here is behavioural rather than a signature: the wearer chooses the wearing style, chooses among the technically valid placements, and is told in plain words that they can stop the visit at any point without argument. Where a caregiver application shares location, activity or alert history with the family, the wearer is shown exactly what is shared, with whom, and that it can be changed. If the wearer refuses, the install does not proceed on the strength of the payer's authority: the refusal is recorded in the wearer's own words, the equipment is left unactivated under the operator's rule, and the commercial question goes back to the sales side. Where a family states that a legal representative holds authority, the installer records their statement rather than assessing anyone's capacity.

included: the doorstep re-consent conversation and its record
the wearer's choice of wearing style and placement within valid options
disclosure of what the centre and the family can hear, see or be told
the recorded-refusal path and the unactivated-equipment rule
excluded: assessing decision-making capacity or cognition
overriding or negotiating around a refusal
price, plan and contract terms, which belong to the acquisition side
consent and sharing changes made later during the live subscription

pros.claim: A wearer who chose the device and its placement actually wears it, which is the only condition under which any of this works
pros.example: a wrist unit chosen by the wearer after she refused a neck cord that reminded her of hospital, and worn every day afterwards

pros.claim: Explicit sharing disclosure prevents the discovery months later that a parent did not know their location was visible to their children
pros.example: showing the caregiver app's location screen at install and agreeing which alerts the family receives

cons.claim: Honouring a refusal cancels revenue already booked and puts the installer in the middle of a family disagreement in someone's living room
cons.example: a son who has driven four hours and wants the base installed regardless of his mother's objection

cons.claim: A consent conversation at the door can feel like re-litigating a decision the family thought was settled, and it slows an already long visit
cons.example: a wearer who becomes anxious when asked again whether she really wants it, after the sale was agreed weeks earlier

failure_modes: installing over an objection because the payer insists and is present
skipping the location and alert-sharing disclosure on a mobile unit or caregiver app
treating a signed sales agreement as consent to enter, drill and attach
recording assent for a wearer who was never actually addressed directly
acceptance_tests: the record shows the wearer was told what is shared and with whom, chose the wearing style and placement, and either assented or refused, addressed directly and in their own presence
any refusal is recorded in the wearer's own words with the equipment left unactivated and the sales side notified
revisit_triggers: the wearer withdraws assent or stops wearing the device
the caregiver application's sharing settings or defaults change
a dispute about who holds authority for the wearer surfaces

base.update_signal: a refusal, a withdrawn assent or a privacy complaint reveals a disclosure that was skipped, or the caregiver app changes what it shares by default

nodes.definition: Walk the whole dwelling with the wearer before deciding anything, mapping where the person actually spends time and where a press is most likely to be needed. The survey records building type and construction, because stucco over lath, a concrete stairwell, foil-backed insulation, a metal-sided workshop and a basement each attenuate radio differently; the floor plan and its levels; the rooms used at three in the morning; the bathroom and shower positions; and the outdoor extent genuinely used, which may be a mailbox at the kerb, a vegetable bed at the back fence, a detached garage or a shared laundry two floors down. It also captures the household facts that change everything downstream: pets that must be shut away before responders enter, a spouse who also needs a button, hearing aids removed at night, a landline that is really a broadband adapter, a security screen that locks from inside. Finally it records the constraints that bound the work without being the installer's business, such as a landlord's ban on drilling, a housing scheme's rules, or a family's objection to a visible box in the hall. The output is a marked plan that the range test walks against, not an impression carried in the technician's head.

included: layout, levels and construction notes that predict radio behaviour
usage geography including the night route and the outdoor extent actually used
household facts and tenancy constraints that bound placement and response
excluded: home-safety assessment or modification recommendations such as grab bars, lighting or rug removal
any judgment about whether the dwelling is suitable for the person
the range measurements themselves, which are the next unit of work

pros.claim: Mapping the night route and the outdoor extent before choosing hardware prevents the classic system that works only in the living room
pros.example: discovering that the wearer carries laundry to a shared basement two floors down, which no in-home pendant will reach

pros.claim: Household facts captured early prevent both wasted trips and dangerous surprises at a real event
pros.example: recording a large dog that must be shut away, so responders are not delayed at the door

cons.claim: A full walk-through costs visit time and can feel intrusive to someone who did not invite an inspection of their bedroom and bathroom
cons.example: a wearer who declines to show the bathroom, leaving the highest-risk room unsurveyed and the map incomplete

cons.claim: The survey captures a moment, and a household's routine and furniture change without anyone reporting it
cons.example: a spare room converted to a bedroom after a hospital stay, changing the night route the survey recorded

failure_modes: surveying only the rooms the family chooses to show
missing a second occupant who also needs coverage
never asking about outdoor routine or the shared parts of a building
recording impressions instead of a marked plan the range test can be walked against
acceptance_tests: the survey record names construction type, every level, the night route, the outdoor extent used and each household or tenancy constraint
any room the wearer declined to show is explicitly marked unsurveyed rather than left blank
revisit_triggers: the household composition, furniture layout or dwelling changes
the wearer's daily routine changes after a hospital stay or a mobility change
a press arrives from a location the survey never listed

base.update_signal: a press or a service visit reveals a used location the survey never recorded, or the household reports a layout, occupancy or routine change

nodes.definition: Decide and prove how a signal will physically leave this building. The candidate paths are a copper telephone line where one genuinely still exists, a cellular radio inside the base or the mobile unit, and a broadband or wireless network path where the device supports one, and each has a different failure geometry. The work is measurement rather than assumption: read the served carrier's signal at the intended base position and at the wearer's bed and bathroom rather than at the front window where it always looks fine; establish whether the household's landline is really voice over broadband delivered by the same modem that dies with the power; check whether the wireless network is a mesh whose password nobody can reproduce after a router reset or a captive network the device cannot join; and identify which candidate paths share a single failure point with each other and with the mains. Where a dwelling offers two paths, prefer the configuration whose failure points do not coincide, such as a cellular radio that survives a broadband outage. Where only a marginal path exists, the honest outcomes are a different device class, a manufacturer-supported antenna or repeater, or declining the install, never shipping a system that signals from the porch but not from the bedroom.

included: signal readings taken at the bed, the bathroom and the base position
identifying voice-over-broadband masquerading as a landline
mapping shared failure points across paths and the mains
the redesign or decline options when coverage is marginal
excluded: repairing, upgrading or advising on the household's broadband or phone service
carrier plan or account advice
the radio link between pendant and base, which is the range unit
the monitoring centre's own network redundancy

pros.claim: Catching a voice-over-broadband line before install prevents a system that is silently dead in every power cut
pros.example: tracing a wall jack back to the cable modem instead of trusting the household's description of a landline

pros.claim: Choosing paths whose failure points do not coincide converts a single outage from an outage of the alarm into an inconvenience
pros.example: keeping a cellular base in a home whose broadband and cordless phones both die with the mains

cons.claim: Honest measurement can disqualify the device the household already bought and force an awkward conversation and a restock
cons.example: two bars at the front door and nothing at the bedside in a steel-framed apartment

cons.claim: A reading is a snapshot: carrier coverage, tower load and household network changes move it after the technician leaves
cons.example: a bedside reading that degrades when the neighbouring building's scaffolding goes up

failure_modes: measuring signal only where the technician happens to be standing
assuming a wall jack means copper
commissioning on a wireless password the household cannot reproduce
ignoring that the chosen path dies with the same power cut as the router
acceptance_tests: the record shows a signal reading or line-type verification at the base position, the bed and the bathroom, with the chosen path named
the shared failure points between the chosen path, the mains and the household's other services are written down
revisit_triggers: the household changes carrier, router, phone service or dwelling
a service visit produces a materially different reading
the carrier retires a network generation the device depends on

base.update_signal: a carrier, router or phone-service change in the household, or a re-measurement that disagrees with the install reading

nodes.definition: Prove where the pendant actually reaches by pressing it at the perimeter of real life, and map where it does not. Published range figures describe open air, while the places a person falls are a far bathroom behind two walls, a basement laundry, a detached garage, a garden gate and a half-landing on the stairs, each attenuating differently. The method is a walk test against the surveyed plan: put the base at its candidate position, then trigger from every named location, including inside the shower with the door closed, at the head of the stairs, at the back fence and at the kerbside mailbox, recording pass, marginal or fail per location rather than one summary number. The pendant is worn as it will be worn, against the body under clothing, because a device held overhead reports a range the wearer will never have. Marginal results are treated as failures until they are resolved by moving the base and re-walking the map, because a signal that sometimes gets through is worse than one that never does: it teaches the wearer to trust it. The output is a dead-spot map that drives base placement, device class and the honest conversation about where this pendant will not help.

included: per-location pass, marginal or fail results with the pendant worn as worn
retesting from alternative base positions when results are marginal
the dead-spot map handed to placement, class selection and training
excluded: the outbound path from base to monitoring centre, which is the connectivity unit
fall-sensor behaviour
any claim of coverage at locations that were never tested

pros.claim: A dead-spot map converts a vague promise into a specific, teachable truth the household can plan around
pros.example: telling a wearer plainly that the back fence is out of range, and agreeing either a mobile unit or a changed gardening routine

pros.claim: Walk testing before mounting exposes the base position that actually works, rather than the one that looked tidy
pros.example: three trial positions in a stone cottage before the upstairs bathroom passes

cons.claim: Honest mapping shrinks the apparent value of the system that was sold and lengthens the visit substantially in large or awkward properties
cons.example: a long walk test in a bungalow with outbuildings that ends by recommending an additional wall button and a changed base position

cons.claim: Radio conditions are not static, so a passing map can degrade with new furniture, appliances or neighbours
cons.example: a new fridge on the other side of the hall wall turning a passing bathroom into a marginal one

failure_modes: testing from the middle of rooms only
testing with the pendant in hand or held high rather than worn
recording a single range OK for the whole dwelling
accepting a marginal result because the visit is running late
acceptance_tests: every location named in the survey has a recorded result taken with the pendant worn as it will be worn
every marginal location is either resolved by relocating the base and re-walking, or documented as a known limit and disclosed to the household
revisit_triggers: the base is moved, or furniture, appliances or renovation change the radio environment
the household reports a press that did not get through
a new wearing style or pendant type is adopted

base.update_signal: a press fails from a location that previously passed, the base is relocated, or the dwelling's radio environment changes

nodes.definition: Establish what this system does when the electricity stops, and prove as much of it as a visit allows. The base draws mains power and holds a backup battery, while the broadband router, the cordless handsets and often the building's entry system hold none, and a mobile unit runs on a charge that a tired or confused wearer may not renew. The work starts with the outlet: choose one that is not controlled by a wall switch, not on a circuit the household turns off at night, not behind furniture that will be pushed back against the plug, and not shared with a vacuum cleaner socket by way of an extension lead. Then pull the plug and watch what actually happens: whether the base changes state audibly or visually, whether it sends an alternating-current loss report that the centre can see, and whether the wearer will understand the sound it makes. Record any backup-duration figure separately and label it manufacturer-stated when nobody has watched this unit run down. The same discipline covers the mobile unit's charging routine, which is designed rather than mentioned: where the cradle lives, whether it sits on a route the wearer already walks each evening, and whether the low-battery warning is audible to someone with age-related hearing loss.

included: outlet selection and its recorded rationale
the observed unplug behaviour and whether a mains-loss report reaches the centre
designing and rehearsing a charging routine for mobile units
separating manufacturer-stated from observed backup duration
excluded: electrical work, rewiring or advice about the home's electrical system
selling generators or uninterruptible supplies
battery replacement scheduling during the live subscription, which belongs to the monitoring side

pros.claim: An unswitched outlet and a rehearsed charging habit remove two of the most common causes of a silently dead system
pros.example: finding the base plugged into a socket controlled by the hall light switch the household turns off every night

pros.claim: Watching the unplug behaviour tells the household what an outage will look and sound like before it happens at three in the morning
pros.example: demonstrating the mains-loss tone so the wearer does not mistake it for a fault and unplug the unit

cons.claim: A genuine backup-duration test takes hours, so the honest record usually has to say the figure is manufacturer-stated and unobserved
cons.example: a stated multi-hour backup that nobody in the business has ever watched run to exhaustion on this model

cons.claim: Charging routines depend on a habit that decays quietly, and the install can only design it, not guarantee it
cons.example: a cradle placed on a bedside table that becomes a book pile within a month

failure_modes: using a switched outlet, a shared extension lead or a socket behind heavy furniture
assuming the broadband router has its own backup
letting a mobile unit go home with no charging place and no rehearsed habit
recording a backup figure as if it had been observed
acceptance_tests: the record names the outlet chosen and why, shows the unplug observation and whether a mains-loss report reached the centre, and labels any backup-duration figure as observed or manufacturer-stated
for a mobile unit, the charging location is chosen with the wearer and the low-battery warning has been heard by the wearer
revisit_triggers: the household rearranges furniture or the base is replugged elsewhere
a power event produces behaviour nobody expected
the manufacturer revises the battery specification or the firmware changes power behaviour

base.update_signal: an outage reveals unexpected behaviour, the base is replugged, or the manufacturer changes the battery or its power firmware

nodes.definition: Match the hardware to the person's hands, habits and preferences using what can be observed at the visit and what the household states, without straying into clinical assessment. The facts that decide fit are practical and visible. Can the wearer press and hold a small button with stiff fingers, or do they need a large low-force button they can hit with a palm? Is a neck cord refused for comfort, appearance, or because of an oxygen line, a catheter or a stoma the family mentions? Will a wrist unit come off at night with the watch, which is when it matters most? Do they shower daily, making water rating and bathroom coverage decisive rather than optional? Do hearing aids come out at bedtime, which decides whether two-way voice from a base across a room can work at all? Is there a tremor or a habit that will produce frequent accidental presses? Is daily charging realistic for someone who has never charged anything in their life? The output is a form-factor and feature recommendation with its reason recorded in observational language. It is not an assessment of the person's health, mobility or safety: the installer records what the household states and what the fitting itself demonstrates, and nothing more.

included: press-force and dexterity fit demonstrated at the visit
wearing-style preference and the reason for any refusal
water exposure routine, hearing and voice-reach implications, charging realism
excluded: fall-risk assessment, mobility scoring or cognitive assessment
recommendations about the person's care or living arrangements
interpreting medical devices or lines beyond noting a comfort constraint the household states

pros.claim: Fitting the button to the hand and the routine is what turns a purchased device into a worn one
pros.example: switching to a large-button wrist unit after watching the wearer fail twice to press a small pendant

pros.claim: Recording fit in observational language keeps a useful record without crossing into clinical characterization
pros.example: noting that the wearer pressed successfully on the second attempt with the palm rather than describing hand function clinically

cons.claim: Preference and reliability sometimes point in opposite directions, and honouring preference can mean accepting a weaker configuration
cons.example: a wearer who insists on removing a wrist unit at night, when night-time bathroom trips are the highest-risk period

cons.claim: Fit is assessed in one calm hour and the person's day varies, so a demonstration is a sample rather than a guarantee
cons.example: a press that succeeds in the afternoon and is much harder for the same person on waking

failure_modes: choosing the form factor for the payer's convenience or the technician's stock
recording a clinical-sounding judgment instead of an observation
ignoring a stated shower routine and fitting a device that is removed at the worst moment
never watching the wearer press the button at all
acceptance_tests: the record shows the wearer physically pressed the proposed button successfully during the visit
the wearing style was chosen by the wearer and the fit rationale is stated in observational terms
revisit_triggers: the wearer stops wearing the device or reports discomfort
the household reports a change in dexterity, hearing aids or daily routine
accidental presses become frequent

base.update_signal: the wearer stops wearing the device, reports discomfort, or the household reports a change in dexterity, hearing or routine

nodes.definition: Choose the device class from what the dwelling and the person actually produced in assessment, not from the tier the household saw advertised. The classes differ in failure geometry rather than merely in price. An in-home base with a worn pendant gives loud two-way voice, mains power with battery backup and a pendant battery measured in years, but only inside a radius this building has now had measured. A mobile cellular unit with location goes everywhere the carrier reaches, at the cost of daily charging, weaker voice in a windy street, location accuracy that varies with sky view and building mass, and dependence on a network that may be thin exactly where the person walks. A hybrid pairs both and doubles the maintenance the household must sustain. The decision rule runs directly off the assessment: where does this wearer actually go, does the measured radio cover it, can they sustain the habit the class demands, and which failure would matter most to this household. Cost is a real constraint and belongs in the conversation as the household's own, already disclosed by the sales side, but never as a reason to overstate what the cheaper class does. When the honest answer is that no available class covers the person's routine, that has to be said plainly.

included: class comparison by failure geometry rather than feature list
the decision rule keyed to measured coverage and sustainable habit
the written statement of the routine the chosen class will not cover
excluded: pricing, plan tiers and contract terms, which arrive disclosed from the acquisition side
brand and supplier economics
recommending a class the assessment does not support in order to reach a subscription tier

pros.claim: Choosing on measured coverage and sustainable habit produces systems that are still in use after the first month rather than in a drawer
pros.example: declining to sell a mobile unit to a wearer who cannot maintain a nightly charge, and covering the same routine with a base plus extra wall buttons

pros.claim: Naming the uncovered routine in writing at selection converts a future complaint into a decision the household made with full information
pros.example: recording that the allotment two streets away is outside coverage and agreeing what the wearer will do there

cons.claim: The class the evidence supports is sometimes the cheaper one, so honest selection reduces both the equipment sale and the subscription tier
cons.example: recommending an in-home system to a housebound wearer whose family had already chosen the flagship mobile plan

cons.claim: A class chosen for today's routine can be wrong within a year as mobility, confidence or living situation changes
cons.example: an in-home base that fits perfectly until the wearer recovers enough to resume daily walks

failure_modes: presenting mobile as strictly better than in-home
ignoring the charging-realism finding because the family likes the mobile unit
leaving the uncovered part of the routine unstated
selecting from van stock rather than from the assessment
acceptance_tests: the selection record cites the specific measurements and fit findings that drove it
the routine the chosen class does not cover is named in writing and acknowledged by the household
revisit_triggers: the wearer's mobility or routine changes materially
measured coverage changes after a carrier, building or furniture change
the household reports regularly using a zone the record listed as uncovered

base.update_signal: a change in the wearer's routine or mobility, a change in measured coverage, or a pattern of accounts abandoning the class chosen

nodes.definition: Explain automatic fall detection as what it is, a sensor and algorithm inference that some falls produce and some do not, and then encode that framing into everything said, sold and written about the feature. The mechanism is unglamorous: accelerometers and pressure sensors infer a fall from an impact-and-stillness signature, so a slow slide down a wall, a fall onto a soft bed or sofa, or any fall while the pendant sits on the nightstand generate nothing at all, while sitting down heavily, dropping the device on tile or an enthusiastic grandchild can generate an alert with no fall behind it. The sentence the installer owes every household is that fall detection supplements pressing the button and never replaces it, and that the press remains the reliable path. This unit also governs the negative claims: no detection percentage is ever quoted, the phrase that it will call for help if you fall is never used, and the feature is never allowed to justify leaving someone alone in circumstances the family would otherwise question. The upside is stated as honestly as the limit, because for a wearer who may be unconscious or unable to press, the sensor is the only path there is, which is precisely why families buy it.

included: the plain-language mechanism explanation and its known blind spots
the supplement-not-substitute sentence and its acknowledgement
prohibited claims, and the honest statement of when the sensor is the only path
excluded: any detection-rate figure or comparative accuracy claim
clinical fall-risk evaluation of the wearer
the verification procedure itself, which is a separate unit
device sensitivity engineering beyond the manufacturer's supported settings

pros.claim: Honest framing prevents the catastrophic expectation gap in which a family experiences an undetected fall as a service failure or a lie
pros.example: a household told at install that a slow slide may not register, so a later unregistered fall is understood rather than litigated

pros.claim: Framing the feature as a supplement keeps the button habit alive, which is the only path that works reliably
pros.example: a wearer who still presses during a dizzy spell instead of waiting for the device to decide something happened

cons.claim: The honest version weakens the feature's headline appeal and can cost the higher subscription tier the family was ready to buy
cons.example: an adult son reconsidering the fall-detection plan once told it cannot be relied on by itself

cons.claim: Repeating the limits can read as hedging, and some households hear it as the installer disowning the product
cons.example: a family asking why they should pay extra for something described as probabilistic

failure_modes: repeating a marketing detection rate as if it were a measurement
describing the feature as automatic protection or as watching over the wearer
allowing the feature to substitute for button training
letting the feature be used to reassure a family out of a care conversation they should be having
acceptance_tests: the install record contains the supplement-not-substitute statement acknowledged by both wearer and caregiver
no detection-rate figure, guarantee or prevention language appears anywhere in the record or the leave-behind material
revisit_triggers: the manufacturer changes sensor hardware or detection algorithm
the household reports recurring false alerts or an undetected fall
new marketing material introduces claims the framing does not support

base.update_signal: a manufacturer sensor or algorithm change, a reported undetected fall, or marketing material that introduces an unsupported claim

nodes.definition: Decide where the hardware physically lives, treating placement as a reliability decision rather than a tidiness one. The base goes where the walk test passed for the whole dwelling and where two-way voice will actually carry to the floor of the bathroom and the far bedroom, which is usually a central hallway rather than a corner of the lounge behind a television. It sits on an unswitched outlet, off the floor, clear of a microwave or a large metal appliance, with its speaker unobstructed and its cable run so that nobody trips over it. Supplementary buttons go where falls concentrate and the pendant may not be worn: beside the shower at a height reachable from the floor rather than from standing, at the head and the foot of the stairs, and beside the bed within arm's reach of someone lying down. The fixing method respects the tenancy, so no drilling where a landlord forbids it, and no adhesive on a surface that will strip paint or fail in bathroom humidity. Placement is also negotiated with the household's dignity, because a box that announces frailty to visitors gets moved or unplugged, so within the options that pass the retest the wearer chooses.

included: base siting against measured coverage and voice reach
supplementary button placement at fall-concentration points and reachable heights
fixing method chosen for tenancy and humidity
the wearer's choice among positions that pass the retest
excluded: general home modification or safety retrofits
electrical or plumbing work
drilling where the tenancy forbids it
accepting a position that fails the retest in exchange for appearance

pros.claim: Placement decided from the dead-spot map and voice reach turns a technically correct install into a usable one
pros.example: moving the base out of a lounge cabinet into the hallway so a call from the bathroom floor is audible in both directions

pros.claim: Buttons placed at fall-concentration points cover the exact moments the pendant is most likely to be off the body
pros.example: a shower button mounted low enough to reach from the floor of the cubicle rather than at light-switch height

cons.claim: The optimal position is frequently the least attractive or least convenient one, and negotiating it takes time and sometimes loses
cons.example: a household insisting the base stay in a spare room, which then has to be recorded as a disclosed coverage compromise

cons.claim: Fixed mountings are semi-permanent decisions made from a single day's information about how a home is used
cons.example: a stair button mounted before the household moves the wearer's bedroom downstairs

failure_modes: placing the base for cable convenience or appearance rather than coverage
mounting a bathroom button at standing height where a fallen person cannot reach it
running a trailing cable across a walkway in a home where falls are the whole concern
fixing anything before the post-placement retest is run
acceptance_tests: after final placement the range test is re-run at the critical locations and passes, and voice audibility is confirmed from the bathroom floor position
the fixing method and any tenancy constraint are recorded, and every supplementary button is reachable from floor level where that is its purpose
revisit_triggers: furniture, room use or the wearer's bedroom changes
the household relocates the base or a button
a call proves inaudible from a room that previously passed

base.update_signal: the base or a button is moved, the household changes room use, or a call proves inaudible from somewhere that previously passed

nodes.definition: Solve the problem that a working alarm still ends at a locked door. The plan establishes how somebody gets in when the wearer is on the floor and cannot open it: a lockbox fixed where responders will actually look with its code recorded in the account, a neighbour or family member holding a key whose availability is real rather than nominal, a building manager or concierge in a managed block, an entry-system or gate code, and any dog that must be shut away before anyone enters. Every element is verified rather than assumed, which means the key is turned in the lock during the visit, the gate code is entered once, and the neighbour is actually asked and agrees rather than being volunteered by a relative. The plan also records the household's own choice between a lockbox and accepting forced entry, because that is a decision with a real security cost on one side and a broken door on the other, and it belongs to the family rather than the installer. Local emergency services, alarm-permit schemes and monitoring centres each have their own conventions about key safes, codes and who may hold them, and those conventions are an obligation class to confirm locally rather than to assume from another jurisdiction.

included: lockbox siting and code capture under the operator's data rule
keyholder confirmation with real availability and consent
gate, building and pet handling instructions
the household's recorded choice about forced entry
excluded: locksmithing, door hardware repair or security-system integration
guaranteeing any emergency service's entry practice
storing codes anywhere other than the monitoring account as the operator's data rule requires

pros.claim: A tested key in a fixed lockbox is what converts a successful alarm into a successful response
pros.example: a code recorded in the account and a key that was physically turned in the lock during the visit, rather than a key someone believes is under a mat

pros.claim: Recording the entry method in the dispatcher-facing record removes minutes of discovery at the moment they cost most
pros.example: an operator able to tell responders the lockbox is on the gas meter box to the left of the porch

cons.claim: A lockbox is a permanent security exposure and some households and buildings refuse them outright, leaving forced entry as the default
cons.example: a family that declines a key safe and accepts in writing that a door may be broken

cons.claim: Access arrangements decay quietly as locks, codes and neighbours change without anyone thinking to report it
cons.example: a gate code changed by the management company months after install and never updated in the account

failure_modes: recording a keyholder who lives an hour away as the primary entry route
saving a key that was never tested in the lock
capturing a code that changed after install and was never revisited
writing a lockbox code somewhere outside the operator's data-handling rule
acceptance_tests: the account holds a verified entry method, proven by turning the key in the lock or entering the code successfully during the visit
the household's choice between a key safe and forced entry is recorded, with the pets and building-access instructions responders will need
revisit_triggers: the household changes locks, gate codes or building management
a keyholder moves, withdraws or becomes unreachable
an incident review shows entry was delayed

base.update_signal: a lock, code, keyholder or building-management change, or an incident review that shows responders were delayed at the door

nodes.definition: Build the account a dispatcher will read at three in the morning, and bind this hardware to it. The work has two halves. The device half is provisioning: registering serial numbers, activating the cellular subscriber identity, pairing the pendant and every supplementary button to the base, applying any pending firmware before the test rather than after it, and confirming the unit reports a supervision check-in under its own account number. The record half is where errors kill people. The dispatch address must be the address responders drive to, complete with unit or apartment number, building name, entry lane and a cross street where rural addressing is ambiguous, and any difference between the billing address and the premises must be resolved explicitly rather than left for an operator to guess. The record also carries the wearer's name and how they wish to be addressed, the language they will answer in, the fact that they may not hear a speaker without hearing aids, the verified entry method and the contact tree. Every field is written for a stranger under time pressure: short, literal, free of internal shorthand. The billing relationship with an adult-child payer is kept separate from the dispatch record so that a payment problem never silently changes who gets called.

included: serial, subscriber-identity and firmware provisioning with a supervision check-in
the dispatch address verified against the premises
wearer identity, language, hearing and entry fields written for a stranger
separation of billing identity from the dispatch record
excluded: subscription pricing, invoicing and billing operations
keeping the record current after go-live, which belongs to the monitoring side
any clinical field authored by the installer
the monitoring platform's own engineering

pros.claim: An address verified against the premises rather than the contract is the single highest-value field in the entire system
pros.example: catching that the agreement carries the daughter's address in another town while the wearer lives in a rear annexe with its own access lane

pros.claim: Fields written for a stranger under pressure are read correctly at the only moment they matter
pros.example: replacing an internal shorthand note with the plain sentence that the wearer does not hear the speaker without hearing aids

cons.claim: Careful record work is invisible when it is right, unglamorous, and competes directly with the visit clock
cons.example: a technician who finishes the physical install in twenty minutes and then rushes the account fields that matter far more

cons.claim: The record is only true on the day it is written, and households move, change names and change access without telling anyone
cons.example: an account still carrying a previous entry code a year after the management company changed it

failure_modes: using the payer's address as the dispatch address
omitting a unit number, building name or access lane
leaving a button unpaired or a device unsupervised after a firmware update
writing internal jargon into a dispatcher-facing note
acceptance_tests: during the end-to-end test the centre reads back the dispatch address, the wearer's name and the entry method, and the read-back matches the premises
the device shows a supervision check-in under the correct account with every button paired and identified
revisit_triggers: any address, entry, identity or contact change
device replacement, subscriber-identity change or firmware update
the monitoring platform changes its field schema or its read-back procedure

base.update_signal: an address, entry, device or identity change, or a read-back at any test that does not match the premises

nodes.definition: Assemble the list of people the centre will call, ordered by who can actually arrive, and verify every entry before it is saved. The failure pattern is close to universal: families list the eldest son first because of seniority, so the centre works an unanswered mobile in another time zone while a neighbour with a key lives three doors away and is not on the list at all. Ordering is therefore by real reachability and proximity, which means who is nearest, who answers at night, who holds a key, and who works shifts underground with no reception, and each entry carries the availability window the household states rather than a single bare number. Every contact is telephoned during the visit, told they have been listed, told what a call from the monitoring centre will mean and what will be asked of them, and given a genuine chance to decline, because a contact who has not agreed is not a contact. Numbers are dialled at the visit to prove they reach a person rather than a disconnected line or a voicemail box that is full. The wearer decides who appears on the list and who is deliberately left off, including family members they do not wish to have called, and that exclusion is recorded and honoured.

included: reachability-based ordering with stated availability windows
a live verification dial and explicit consent for every entry
relationship and keyholder status per contact
the wearer's right to exclude a family member
excluded: obliging any contact to respond to a call
adjudicating family disputes about who should be listed
keeping the tree current after go-live, which belongs to the monitoring side
emergency-services dispatch policy itself

pros.claim: A verified, consented, proximity-ordered tree is the difference between a door opened in minutes and a chain of voicemail
pros.example: promoting a next-door neighbour who holds a key above an out-of-state son after both were telephoned during the visit

pros.claim: Telling each contact in advance what a call will mean removes the confusion and hesitation that costs minutes at the real event
pros.example: a night contact who already knows she will be asked to go round and let responders in

cons.claim: Verification calls are intrusive and slow, and some relatives resent learning they have been listed only when the technician telephones them
cons.example: a daughter-in-law told during the install that she is the primary night contact, having never been asked

cons.claim: Reachability ordering can contradict family hierarchy and place the installer inside a dispute that is not theirs
cons.example: an eldest son who objects to being listed below a neighbour

failure_modes: ordering by seniority or by who is paying
saving numbers that were never dialled
listing a person who never agreed to be called
recording no availability window for a shift worker or a frequent traveller
acceptance_tests: every saved contact was dialled during the visit, reached a person, and that person agreed to be listed
each entry carries relationship, availability window and keyholder status, and the ordering rationale is reachability rather than rank
revisit_triggers: a contact moves, changes number or withdraws consent
a real event shows the order failed to produce anyone
the wearer asks to add, remove or reorder someone

base.update_signal: a contact changes number, moves or withdraws, or an event shows the call order produced nobody

nodes.definition: Configure what the monitoring centre actually does when this account's signal arrives, inside the protocols that centre operates. The default sequence, which is roughly to attempt two-way voice, redial the premises, work the contact tree and request emergency dispatch when no contact is made, is then modified per account by facts the household supplies: dispatch immediately without working the tree because the wearer cannot speak, call the daughter first between stated hours, never call one particular number, treat silence as presence rather than absence because hearing aids come out at night, or handle a fall alert differently from a button press. Two disciplines govern the work. First, every instruction must be one the centre's platform can actually hold and its operators will actually follow, confirmed with the centre rather than promised to the family in the living room. Second, the installer transcribes the household's instructions and never authors clinical ones: a family's statement about resuscitation preferences or a condition is recorded as their statement, if the centre accepts such a field at all, and any question about what they ought to instruct goes back to their clinician. What the centre will not do is stated to the household as plainly as what it will.

included: per-account modifications to the centre's default sequence
confirmation that each instruction is supportable by the platform and the operators
transcription discipline for household-supplied medical statements
the explicit statement of what the centre will not do
excluded: the centre's internal operating procedures, staffing and training
advising a family what their medical or dispatch instructions ought to be
any instruction the platform cannot hold
protocol changes made after go-live, which belong to the monitoring side

pros.claim: Protocol tuned to the household's real situation prevents both the delayed dispatch and the unwanted one
pros.example: an instruction that silence on an alert means dispatch, for a wearer who removes hearing aids at night

pros.claim: Confirming each instruction with the centre first keeps the family's expectations and the centre's behaviour identical
pros.example: discovering that a requested do-not-call restriction cannot be held on the platform, and redesigning the tree instead of promising it

cons.claim: Every special instruction adds a way for the response to go wrong under a different operator on a different shift, so complexity is itself a risk
cons.example: a time-of-day contact rule misapplied across a daylight-saving change

cons.claim: Instruction sets grow faster than they are pruned, and a dispatcher will not read a screen of them under pressure
cons.example: an account carrying six conditional rules where two would have produced a better response

failure_modes: promising a behaviour the centre cannot configure
an installer-authored clinical instruction in a dispatcher-facing field
so many instructions that no operator can act on them in seconds
never telling the household what the centre will not do
acceptance_tests: each configured instruction is confirmed as supported by the monitoring centre and appears in the account as configured
the household is told in writing what the centre will not do, and the medical statements in the record are in the household's own words
revisit_triggers: the centre changes protocol, platform or operator procedure
the household's instructions or circumstances change
a real event shows an instruction was not followed or produced a harmful outcome

base.update_signal: the centre changes its protocol or platform, the household changes its instructions, or an event shows an instruction was not followed

nodes.definition: Prove the whole chain in one sequence before the van leaves, because every upstream unit of work is a hypothesis until a real signal completes a real path. This is not a button press with a green light. It is a press from a genuinely hard location, the bathroom floor position rather than beside the base, confirmed as received at the centre; a two-way conversation held from that position at floor level, with the wearer hearing the operator and the operator hearing the wearer without anyone shouting; an operator read-back of the account exactly as it will be used, covering the dispatch address, the wearer's name, the entry method and the first contact; a trigger of every supplementary button with each arriving distinctly identified; confirmation that the signal is flagged as a test and logged with its timestamp; and, for a mobile unit, a repeat outside the property so the cellular and location path is exercised where the wearer actually goes. Any failure ends the test rather than the account: the fault is fixed and the whole sequence is repeated from the first press rather than resumed in the middle. A partially passed test is a failed test, because the parts that were skipped are exactly the parts nobody has proven.

included: the hard-location press and floor-level two-way voice leg
the operator read-back of the live record
distinct identification of every button, test flagging and logging
the off-premise leg for mobile units and the full repeat after any fix
excluded: simulating a real fall on the wearer's body
measuring the centre's staffing or long-run answer performance
periodic test calls during the live subscription, which belong to the monitoring side

pros.claim: The read-back leg catches record errors that no amount of equipment testing would ever reveal
pros.example: an operator reading back a dispatch address with no apartment number, caught while the technician is still standing in the apartment

pros.claim: A floor-level voice leg tests the system in the posture of the emergency rather than the posture of the demonstration
pros.example: discovering that the wearer cannot hear the operator from the bathroom floor with the door closed, which a standing test would have passed

cons.claim: A full test occupies monitoring-centre operator time and lengthens the visit, and the pressure to shorten it is constant and worst on the last job of the day
cons.example: skipping the off-premise leg for a mobile unit because it started raining

cons.claim: The test proves the chain at one moment in one configuration and cannot prove it will still hold next month
cons.example: a passing test in a home where the base is later moved by a cleaner

failure_modes: testing from beside the base rather than from a hard location
accepting a marginal or shouted voice result
resuming a test after a fix instead of repeating the sequence
failing to flag the signal as a test so it enters the account history as a real event
acceptance_tests: the log shows a completed sequence with location, timestamp, the read-back items confirmed, every button distinctly identified, and the off-premise leg where a mobile unit is involved
any earlier failed attempt is retained in the record with the fault found and the fix applied
revisit_triggers: any hardware, firmware, address, contact or protocol change
a device replacement or a base relocation
an event suggesting some part of the path did not work

base.update_signal: any configuration, hardware or record change after the test, or an event indicating a leg of the path failed in service

nodes.definition: Verify the fall-detection feature to the exact extent it can be verified, and document the rest as untested. What can be done safely is the manufacturer's prescribed check, typically a controlled drop of the device itself from a stated height onto a stated surface or a diagnostic self-test mode, confirming three things: that a detected event produces an alert at the centre, that the alert is distinguishable in the account from an ordinary button press so the operator knows which happened, and that the cancel window works so the wearer can stand up and stop a false alarm before anyone is called. What must never be done is asking an older adult to fall, or to lie on the floor pretending to have fallen. What cannot be established at all in a living room is whether this particular person's real falls will be detected, and that gap is written into the record in the same words that were used aloud during the framing conversation. The cancel behaviour deserves its own rehearsal, because the first false alert usually arrives within days and a wearer who does not know how to cancel one learns instead to take the device off.

included: the manufacturer's prescribed device-level check
distinguishability of a fall alert from a button press in the account
cancel-window rehearsal performed by the wearer
the written statement of what remains unverified
excluded: any simulated fall involving the wearer's body
detection-rate measurement or any accuracy claim
clinical interpretation of the wearer's fall risk
sensitivity changes outside the manufacturer's supported settings

pros.claim: Rehearsing the cancel window at install prevents the abandonment spiral that follows the first embarrassing false alert
pros.example: a wearer who cancels a false alert calmly from the sofa a week later instead of unplugging the base in frustration

pros.claim: Confirming that a fall alert is distinguishable from a press means the operator knows which conversation to have
pros.example: an account where a fall alert triggers the agreed silence-means-dispatch rule while a press does not

cons.claim: The honest record must state that real-fall detection was not verified, which reads as weakness to a family who paid extra for the feature
cons.example: a caregiver asking why the installer cannot simply demonstrate that it works

cons.claim: A device-level check says nothing about how the sensor behaves on this person's body, gait and daily movement
cons.example: a unit that passes the drop check and then alerts twice a week when its wearer sits down heavily

failure_modes: skipping the check because the feature is considered standard
letting a family member simulate a fall to demonstrate it
recording the device check as evidence that the wearer's falls will be detected
never rehearsing the cancel window
acceptance_tests: the log shows the manufacturer-prescribed check completed with the alert received and distinguishable from a press
the cancel rehearsal was performed by the wearer, and an explicit unverified statement about real-fall detection is in the record
revisit_triggers: firmware or sensor revision changes detection behaviour
repeated false alerts or a reported undetected fall
the manufacturer changes its prescribed check procedure

base.update_signal: a firmware or sensor revision, a reported undetected fall, or a pattern of false alerts in the field

nodes.definition: Train the person who will press the button until they demonstrate it, rather than until the installer has finished explaining. The content is small and specific: press and hold for this long; press for anything you would call for help about, including a fall you could get up from, chest pain, a stranger at the door or feeling unwell in the night; the box will talk to you and the voice is a real person; you do not need to reach the base or the telephone; nobody is annoyed by a false alarm and this is how you cancel one; wear it in the shower, because that is where it matters most; and, for a mobile unit, charge it here, at this time, every day. The method is teach-back and demonstration rather than explanation: the wearer presses it themselves from the bathroom, speaks with the operator, cancels a test alert and states in their own words when they would press it. Two habits are trained explicitly because they are the ones that decay first, which are wearing it at night and pressing rather than waiting to see whether the feeling passes. The training is pitched to hearing and eyesight, spoken slowly and face-on with a large-print card left behind, and it is addressed to the wearer even when a relative keeps answering on their behalf.
