included: the wearer's own demonstrated press from a hard location
when-to-press criteria restated in the wearer's own words
false-alarm reassurance and cancel practice
shower and night wearing habits, charging habit for mobile units, large-print leave-behind
excluded: instructing on any medical matter or on when to seek clinical care
the family's ongoing responsibilities, which are the caregiver briefing
refresher training during the live subscription, which belongs to the monitoring side

pros.claim: Teach-back turns a passive briefing into evidence and exposes the wearer who did not hear a word of it
pros.example: a wearer who says she would press it if she could not get up but not for a little fall, which is exactly the belief that must be corrected before the visit ends

pros.claim: Practising the cancel makes a false alarm cheap, which is what keeps the device on the body
pros.example: a wearer who has already cancelled one test alert and is therefore unafraid of pressing

cons.claim: Training time competes with the visit clock and adult children answer for the wearer, producing a trained family and an untrained wearer
cons.example: a son who says she has got it after the third question his mother has not answered

cons.claim: A demonstration on install day is not a habit, and both wearing and pressing decay in the weeks afterwards
cons.example: a pendant left on the bedside table within a fortnight because nothing has happened yet

failure_modes: explaining rather than requiring a demonstration
training the caregiver instead of the wearer
leaving without correcting a wait-and-see belief
no cancel practice and no large-print card
acceptance_tests: the wearer independently completed a press from the bathroom, spoke with the operator, cancelled a test alert and stated when they would press it in their own words
the leave-behind card is large print, in the wearer's language, and carries the centre's number and the cancel instruction
revisit_triggers: the wearer reports not wearing it or hesitating to press
a real event in which the button was available and not used
a device or feature change that alters how the press or cancel works

base.update_signal: a report that the wearer is not wearing or not pressing the device, or an event where the button was available and unused

nodes.definition: Brief the family at the end of the visit on what they have actually bought, in terms that will hold up when something goes wrong. The content is deliberately unflattering. This is signaling equipment and a monitoring service, not supervision and not care; nobody is watching a screen; a fall may not be detected; the device only works when it is worn, charged and in range, and here is the map of where it is not. The family also receives the operating facts they will need: how to reach the centre, that changes of address, contacts, entry codes and phone service must be reported and exactly how to report them, what a periodic test call is and why it will happen, and how cancellation works, stated plainly rather than buried. Where a caregiver application exists, its notifications are demonstrated together with what the wearer agreed to share and what they did not. Each contact is told what their position in the tree means in practice. The orientation closes the install's family-facing work and hands the relationship to the monitoring side, and it deliberately does not open the ongoing communication rhythm, which belongs there.

included: the not-supervision statement and the wearing, charging and coverage dependencies
what each contact's position in the tree means in practice
how to report changes, what a test call is, and the plain cancellation route
caregiver-app demonstration within the wearer's consent
excluded: the ongoing caregiver relationship, check-in cadence and retention conversations
renegotiating the plan, price or contract
any clinical guidance about the wearer's care or living arrangements

pros.claim: An honest, deflating briefing at install is the cheapest insurance against the expectation gap that turns a normal limitation into a betrayal
pros.example: a family told plainly that nobody watches a screen, so a quiet month is understood rather than experienced as neglect

pros.claim: Telling the family how to report a change is what keeps the dispatch record true after the technician leaves
pros.example: a daughter who telephones the centre the week the entry code changes because she was told exactly how

cons.claim: The briefing lands at the end of a long visit when everyone is tired, and its most important content is the least welcome
cons.example: a daughter who hears that her mother may fall without it being detected and feels sold something weaker than she believed

cons.claim: Only the family members present are briefed, and the ones who arrive later inherit the marketing version instead
cons.example: a second son abroad who believes the service includes someone watching over his mother

failure_modes: letting the sales brochure's tone carry into the briefing
skipping the change-reporting instruction because time has run out
briefing only whichever relative happens to be in the room
presenting cancellation as difficult or leaving it unmentioned
acceptance_tests: the family acknowledges in the record the not-supervision statement, the wearing, charging and coverage dependencies, and their own position in the contact tree
the change-reporting route and the cancellation route are given in writing on the household card
revisit_triggers: the family composition or the primary caregiver changes
a complaint reveals an expectation the briefing failed to set
the caregiver application or the service's terms change

base.update_signal: a complaint or a service-recovery review showing an expectation the briefing did not set, or a change in the caregiver app or service terms

nodes.definition: Run the same protocol when nobody enters the home, because a shipped device is a common case and the temptation is to let the box be the installation. The guided call reproduces every mandatory element with the household acting as the technician's hands: a room-by-room description that builds the survey; a walk test in which a family member or the wearer presses from the bathroom, the bedroom, the garden gate and the stairs while the technician confirms each arrival at the centre; a plug-in check on an outlet whose wall switch is physically tested; address and entry verification by asking what is written on the door and how a stranger would actually get in; contacts dialled and consented from the office; the same operator read-back and floor-level voice leg; and the same teach-back with the wearer rather than with the relative holding the telephone. The differences must be admitted rather than glossed: nobody has seen the construction, nobody has confirmed the base is not inside a cabinet, and mounting quality is unverified. Those gaps go into the record as named unverified items with a follow-up call inside a defined window that re-tests rather than assumes. Where the protocol cannot complete, because a room cannot be reached, no contact will consent, or the wearer cannot hear the operator, the honest outcomes are a site visit or a return of the equipment, never a partial go-live.

included: the guided walk test with arrival confirmation at the centre
remote address and entry verification questions
identical read-back, voice and teach-back requirements
the named unverified-item list, the follow-up re-test window and the stop condition
excluded: waiving any mandatory test because the install was remote
assessing construction or mounting quality sight-unseen
on-site electrical, mounting or access work

pros.claim: A disciplined remote protocol makes distance a cost rather than a compromise and serves households no technician can reach economically
pros.example: an out-of-area wearer walked through a full bathroom-floor voice test by telephone, with the operator confirming each arrival

pros.claim: Naming the unverified items converts unavoidable uncertainty into a scheduled task instead of a hidden assumption
pros.example: a follow-up call a fortnight later that discovers the base was moved into a cabinet and corrects it

cons.claim: Everything depends on a relative's accuracy and patience, and some things simply cannot be verified from an office, so residual risk is genuinely higher
cons.example: a base the household describes as in the hall that in fact sits inside a closed cupboard

cons.claim: Guided calls take longer than an on-site install and fail more often part-way, consuming office time with no completed account
cons.example: a call abandoned when the wearer cannot hear the operator and no site visit is economic

failure_modes: shipping with a leaflet and treating the delivery as an installation
letting the relative press the button and speak instead of the wearer
skipping the off-premise leg for a mobile unit because nobody is there to walk outside
no unverified-item list and no scheduled re-test
acceptance_tests: the remote install record contains the same completed test log, read-back and teach-back evidence an on-site install would carry
an explicit list of items that could not be verified exists, with a scheduled re-test date and the stop condition applied where a mandatory element failed
revisit_triggers: the follow-up re-test finds a fault or contradicts an assumption
the household reports a placement or coverage problem
the shipped hardware or the manufacturer's setup flow changes

base.update_signal: a follow-up re-test that contradicts what the household reported, or a change in the shipped hardware or its guided setup flow

nodes.definition: Produce the record that lets a stranger reconstruct this installation, and the single piece of paper the household can actually use. The internal record holds the survey and its constraints, the measured connectivity readings, the dead-spot map with its per-location results, the outlet and placement decisions with their reasons, device serials and firmware state, the account fields as configured, the contact tree with its verification and consent evidence, the entry plan with the tested method, the full test log with timestamps including any failed attempt and the fix applied, the fall-detection check with its explicit unverified statement, the teach-back evidence, and the caregiver acknowledgements. The household's copy is different in kind: one large-print card carrying the centre's number, the account number, how to cancel a false alarm, the charging routine where there is one, how to report a change of address, contact or entry code, and a plain statement of the coverage limits found in this home. The purpose is not compliance theatre. It is the artifact the monitoring side inherits, the evidence when a family later disputes what was promised, and the baseline that makes any subsequent change detectable.

included: the internal reconstruction record including measurements, decisions, evidence and failures
the large-print household card with the cancel, change-reporting and coverage-limit content
the baseline handed to the monitoring side
excluded: contract, pricing and billing documents, which belong to the acquisition side
service records created after go-live
storing entry codes, key locations or personal data outside the operator's stated data-handling rule

pros.claim: A record containing measurements and failures is the only defensible answer when an incident is reviewed months later
pros.example: producing a dated dead-spot map showing the back fence was tested, failed and disclosed at install

pros.claim: A single large-print card is the only documentation an older adult will actually use in a moment of confusion
pros.example: a wearer reading the cancel instruction off the card during her first false alarm instead of unplugging the base

cons.claim: Thorough documentation adds real time to every visit and decays in value quickly if nobody downstream reads it
cons.example: a dead-spot map filed and never consulted when the base is later moved by a cleaner

cons.claim: Records that hold entry codes and household detail are themselves a data risk that has to be managed for the life of the account
cons.example: an installer's tablet carrying key-safe codes for a whole route

failure_modes: recording only the successes and deleting the failed test attempt
a leave-behind card in small print or in a language the wearer does not read
storing codes or key locations outside the agreed system
a record so long that the monitoring side never reads the parts that matter
acceptance_tests: an independent reader can reconstruct device, placement, coverage, account, contacts, entry and test results from the record alone
the household card is large print, in the wearer's language, and states the coverage limits found in this home
revisit_triggers: any configuration, contact or entry change
a dispute, complaint or incident review
a change in the operator's data-handling rule or the monitoring platform

base.update_signal: an incident review or a monitoring-side complaint that the record could not answer, or a change to the data-handling rule or platform

nodes.definition: Decide, against a fixed list rather than a feeling, whether this account goes live and transfers to the monitoring side or whether the visit ends unfinished. The gate is binary and its conditions are the outputs of everything upstream: wearer assent recorded; device class justified by measured findings with the uncovered routine stated in writing; the signal path measured where the wearer sleeps and bathes; the dead-spot map complete with marginal locations resolved or disclosed; base and buttons placed with the post-placement retest passed and voice audible from the bathroom floor; an unswitched outlet confirmed; the dispatch address verified against the premises; the entry method tested; the contact tree dialled, consented and ordered by reachability; response instructions confirmed supportable by the centre; the end-to-end test passed in one uninterrupted sequence including read-back; the fall-detection check completed with its limit written; the wearer's teach-back demonstrated; the caregiver briefing acknowledged; and the documentation packet complete with the household card left behind. Anything unmet has exactly two honest outcomes, which are to fix it now or to leave the account not live with the open item, the reason and the return date recorded and told to the household. There is no partially live account, because a family must never believe help is one press away when it is not.

included: the binary condition list and its artifact references
the fix-now-or-not-live rule with a recorded open item and return date
the household notification when an account is left not live
the transfer package handed to the monitoring side
excluded: ongoing monitoring, test-call cadence and account maintenance after transfer
commercial decisions about refunds, credits or rescheduling
waiving any condition for commercial convenience

pros.claim: A binary gate removes the judgement call at the end of a long day, which is exactly when judgement is least reliable
pros.example: a technician at seven in the evening leaving an account not live because the second contact never answered, rather than promising to add them tomorrow

pros.claim: An artifact per condition makes the handover to the monitoring side a transfer of evidence rather than of assurances
pros.example: the monitoring side inheriting a test log and a dead-spot map instead of a note saying installed and working

cons.claim: The gate produces revisits and unbilled hours, and the pressure to soften it grows with volume and with a thin schedule
cons.example: a second trip required because an apartment's bedside cellular reading failed after the base was finally sited

cons.claim: A long condition list can be walked mechanically, producing ticks without the underlying evidence unless artifacts are actually checked
cons.example: a checklist marked complete where the read-back item was never confirmed by the operator

failure_modes: going live with an open item on the strength of a promise
telling the household the system is working while the account is still pending at the centre
recording an open item with no return date and no owner
waiving a condition because the customer is unhappy about a second visit
acceptance_tests: every gate condition maps to a named artifact in the record rather than to a tick
any account left not live carries the failed condition, the household's written notification and a return date with an owner
revisit_triggers: the condition list changes or a new device class is adopted
an incident traces back to a condition that was waived or missing
the monitoring side reports incoming accounts with unusable fields

base.update_signal: an incident that traces to a waived or missing condition, or the monitoring side reporting incoming accounts that cannot be serviced from the record

edges.why_related: the charter makes wearer assent a condition of doing any work in the home, so the doorstep consent step exists because the scope says an install without it is not an install
walking a person's bedroom and bathroom with a clipboard is only legitimate once they have agreed to the visit and know what is being recorded
the survey identifies the rooms that must have usable signal and the wiring and service facts the path assessment then verifies rather than assumes
the walk test is run against the surveyed plan, so the list of locations to press from comes entirely from the survey
shower routine, night route, second occupants and the household's own account of habits are captured in the survey and are what the fit decision is made from
measured signal at the bed and the bathroom decides whether a cellular class is viable at all in this building
the dead-spot map is the evidence that an in-home class covers the wearer's routine or fails to, which is the central selection question
charging realism, water exposure and press capability are half the selection rule, because a class that demands a habit the wearer cannot sustain does not work regardless of coverage
the framing of fall detection is a direct application of the measure-before-claim rule to a feature whose performance cannot be measured at an install
what gets mounted, and whether anything is mounted at all, follows from the class chosen: a base and wall buttons, a charging cradle, or both
the account is provisioned for specific hardware, so serials, subscriber identity, supervision and the alert types the centre will see all follow the class
the verified entry method, lockbox position, gate code and pet instruction are fields in the dispatcher-facing record and are useless anywhere else
contacts are attached to an existing account record, and the ordering only means anything once the dispatch address and wearer identity it serves are fixed
the instructions modify a sequence that works the tree, so who is on the list and when they are available determines which modifications are even coherent
the test must be run from the final positions of base, buttons and cradle, because a test from a trial position proves nothing about the installed system
the operator read-back leg confirms the configured instructions and contact order as the centre actually holds them, which requires the configuration to exist first
training uses the proven system: the wearer's own press during the test is both the first verification leg and the first lesson, and training on an unproven chain teaches a false habit
the test log with its locations, timestamps, read-back items and any failed attempt is the core of the record a stranger later reconstructs the install from
the remote protocol is defined as the same test executed through the household, so its requirements are inherited wholesale from the on-site sequence
what is checked, and the wording of the unverified statement that accompanies the check, are set by the framing agreed with the household beforehand
the family briefing describes what the wearer was actually trained to do and where the training landed, including any belief that had to be corrected
the gate is checked against artifacts rather than recollection, so the packet is the evidence base the binary decision is made from and the parcel the monitoring side inherits
fit assessment sits closest to the clinical line, so the boundary limits it to what the fitting demonstrates and what the household states, in observational language
medical statements in dispatcher-facing fields must be the household's own words, and any question about what they ought to instruct is referred rather than answered
backup duration is the property most often quoted and least often observed, so the rule forces the record to separate what was watched from what the manufacturer states
the wearer decides who may be called and who is deliberately excluded, which bounds the tree regardless of who is paying or who volunteers
the gate is the enforcement point for the charter's stop rules, so it can only contain conditions the charter defined and cannot waive them for commercial convenience
the class the coverage evidence supports and the form factor the wearer will actually wear regularly point in different directions, particularly for mobile units that demand daily charging
edges.resolution_rule: wearability decides the form factor and measured coverage decides the class; where the wearer will not sustain what the coverage requires, the design is changed by adding fixed buttons or a second device, or the gap is disclosed in writing, and wearer compliance is never simply assumed

edges.why_related: the position that passes the retest and carries voice to the bathroom floor is often the visible hallway position the household finds embarrassing
edges.resolution_rule: coverage-critical constraints are stated as non-negotiable and the wearer chooses freely among the positions that pass the post-placement retest; if the household insists on a failing position it is recorded as a disclosed coverage compromise and the gate condition is still not waived

edges.why_related: a guided call cannot observe construction, base position or mounting quality, yet the test requirements do not soften because nobody travelled
edges.resolution_rule: test requirements are identical and only the means of execution differ; every element that cannot be executed remotely is recorded as a named unverified item with a scheduled re-test, and a mandatory element that cannot be completed forces a site visit or the equipment's return rather than a waiver

edges.why_related: honest framing suppresses the feature that most often justifies the higher-priced class and subscription tier the household was ready to buy
edges.resolution_rule: framing dominates the sale: the feature may only be selected with the supplement-not-substitute statement acknowledged by wearer and caregiver, and the tier decision then goes back to the household with that statement in hand rather than being carried by the installer's enthusiasm

edges.why_related: the wearer sometimes excludes a family member the paying adult child insists must be called first, and both are in the room
edges.resolution_rule: the wearer's exclusion governs who the centre calls; the payer's concern is handled by the sales or monitoring side, or by declining the account, and the installer never overrides the wearer's list in their own home

edges.why_related: a button that fits the hand and a wearing style the person chose are what make the teach-back demonstration succeed, so a failed demonstration is usually a fit problem wearing the costume of a training problem
the chosen signal path determines what a power cut actually kills, because a broadband-delivered path dies with the router while a cellular radio on a charged base does not
household facts recorded in the survey, such as hearing aids removed at night, a dog, a second occupant or a locked security screen, are what produce the per-account instruction modifications
a failed arrival or an inaudible floor-level voice leg sends the base or a button back to be repositioned, after which the whole test sequence restarts
a condition that fails repeatedly across installs, or an incident traced to something the list never required, rewrites the charter's definition of a completed install
the family acknowledgements are collected at the end of the briefing and are the last items added before the packet is closed and the household card handed over
both are radio verifications on different links of the same chain and share one method and one record discipline: measure where it matters, record per location, and treat marginal as failing

conflict_axes.name: measured_coverage_vs_preserving_the_sale
conflict_axes.description: The measurements taken in the home regularly contradict the device class and plan tier the household already chose, and the installer is the person holding both the meter and the invoice.
poles: report what was measured and redesign or decline
install the configuration that was sold
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the measurement governs the configuration; the commercial question is reopened with the household and the sales side, and the record is never adjusted to match the invoice

conflict_axes.name: wearer_autonomy_vs_payer_authority
conflict_axes.description: The adult child usually pays, arranges the visit and directs the technician, while the person whose home, body and habits are being changed may want less of it or none of it.
poles: the wearer's assent and preference decide
the payer who arranged and funded the install decides
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: assent and wearing choices belong to the wearer and a refusal stops the install; the payer's concerns are answered by the sales and retention sides, never by overriding the wearer in their own home

conflict_axes.name: family_reassurance_vs_honest_limits
conflict_axes.description: Families want to be told the device will keep their parent safe; the truthful account is a list of conditions, dead spots and probabilistic sensors.
poles: give the reassurance the family came for
state every limit that was found
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: limits are stated in full and in writing, and the reassurance offered is the specific, true one - what was measured, what was tested, and what the household can do about the gaps

conflict_axes.name: visit_clock_vs_complete_verification
conflict_axes.description: Full verification consumes the visit and the monitoring centre's operator time, and the pressure to shorten it peaks on the last job of the day, which is exactly when errors are most likely.
poles: finish the route and bill the day
complete every measurement, test and record
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the go-live conditions are not negotiable against the clock; an install that cannot be completed is left not live with the open item, the reason and a return date recorded and communicated

conflict_axes.name: household_dignity_vs_technical_optimum
conflict_axes.description: The best base position and the most reliable wearing style are often the ones that announce frailty to visitors, and a device that embarrasses its owner gets unplugged or left in a drawer.
poles: place and fit for maximum measured reliability
place and fit for what the wearer will accept living with
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: coverage-critical constraints are stated as non-negotiable, and among the options that pass the post-placement retest the wearer chooses; an insisted-on failing position is recorded as a disclosed coverage compromise rather than quietly accepted

conflict_axes.name: entry_security_vs_entry_speed
conflict_axes.description: A lockbox with a key is the fastest route through a locked door and also a permanent security exposure the household lives with every day.
poles: fix a lockbox and record the code
accept forced entry and its damage
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the trade-off is presented with both costs and decided by the household in writing; whichever is chosen must be verified during the visit and recorded in the account, never left as an assumption

conflict_axes.name: remote_reach_vs_verification_depth
conflict_axes.description: Guided remote setup serves households no technician can reach economically, but nobody has seen the building, the base position or the mounting.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: test requirements are identical and only the means of execution differ; anything that cannot be executed remotely becomes a written unverified item with a scheduled re-test, and a mandatory element that cannot be completed forces a site visit or a return of the equipment

conflict_axes.name: being_helpful_vs_the_non_clinical_boundary
conflict_axes.description: The installer is often the only person in the house who seems knowledgeable, and the questions that follow are about falls, medication, driving and whether mum should still live alone.
poles: answer only the equipment question and refer the rest
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the equipment half is answered fully and the clinical half is referred to the physician, discharge planner or care manager with the referral logged; account fields carry the family's own words, never an installer-authored clinical characterization

conflict_axes.name: false_alarm_tolerance_vs_hesitation_to_press
conflict_axes.description: Training someone to press freely produces false alarms that cost centre time and embarrass the wearer; discouraging false alarms produces the far worse failure of a person who waits to see whether the feeling passes.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: willingness dominates: press-for-anything is trained explicitly, the cancel procedure is rehearsed so a false alarm is cheap and unembarrassing, and false-alarm volume is managed through device settings and fit rather than through wearer hesitation

edge_cases.description: The jack on the wall is not copper: the household's 'landline' is delivered by the same cable modem that dies in a power cut, so the signaling path and the outage backup share one failure point
edge_cases.trigger: a phone jack is present but the service is broadband-delivered voice
edge_cases.mitigation: trace the line to its termination rather than trusting the bill, move to a cellular path or a device class that carries its own radio, and record the finding and the change in the install record

edge_cases.description: The account carries a street address with no unit number in a large apartment block, so a signal that reaches the centre still sends responders to a lobby
edge_cases.trigger: a multi-unit dwelling where the contract address omits the unit, building or entry lane
edge_cases.mitigation: verify the address by what is written on the door and how a stranger would reach it, correct the record at the centre, and confirm it in the operator read-back before the test is accepted

edge_cases.description: The wearer refuses the device at the door after the adult child has paid for it and travelled a long way for the appointment
edge_cases.trigger: the wearer declines to have the equipment installed or worn
edge_cases.mitigation: stop the install, record the refusal in the wearer's own words, leave the equipment unactivated per the operator's rule, tell the payer plainly that the account is not live, and return the commercial question to the sales side

edge_cases.description: Two occupants in the home both need a button but only one pendant and one account were sold
edge_cases.trigger: a spouse or sibling in the same dwelling also wants coverage
edge_cases.mitigation: never let two people share one pendant; each wearer needs a separately identified device at the centre so the operator knows who pressed, which is a configuration and commercial change referred back before go-live

edge_cases.description: Cellular signal is strong at the front door and unusable at the bedside in a steel-framed or basement dwelling
edge_cases.trigger: signal readings vary sharply between the entrance and the rooms the wearer occupies
edge_cases.mitigation: decide on the bedside and bathroom readings, not the doorway reading; relocate the base, use a manufacturer-supported antenna or repeater, change class, or decline the install rather than ship a system that signals only from the porch

edge_cases.description: The wearer removes hearing aids at night, so two-way voice from a base across the room cannot work during the highest-risk hours
edge_cases.trigger: hearing assistance is used by day and removed at night
edge_cases.mitigation: record the fact in the dispatcher-facing record, configure the instruction that silence must not be read as absence, test voice at floor level in the night configuration, and consider a wearable with its own speaker near the wearer

edge_cases.description: The only contact the family offers is an out-of-area adult child whose voicemail box is full
edge_cases.trigger: the contact tree cannot be populated with anyone reachable or local
edge_cases.mitigation: do not go live on a single unverified contact; recruit a local keyholder or neighbour with consent, or configure the account for direct dispatch and tell the household in writing that is what will happen

edge_cases.description: The building bans key safes or the household refuses one, leaving a locked door between a working alarm and the wearer
edge_cases.trigger: no lockbox is permitted or accepted and no keyholder is reliably available
edge_cases.mitigation: record the household's acceptance of forced entry and its damage cost in writing, pursue the building manager or concierge route where one exists, and note the entry method in the dispatcher-facing record so no time is lost discovering it

edge_cases.description: Fall detection alerts repeatedly in the first week from heavy sitting or a pendant dropped on a tiled floor
edge_cases.trigger: recurring false fall alerts after go-live
edge_cases.mitigation: rehearse the cancel window again, adjust wearing style or sensitivity only within the manufacturer's supported settings, escalate a genuinely faulty unit, and never quietly disable the feature the household is paying for without telling them

edge_cases.description: The wearer has significant memory impairment and cannot complete teach-back or reliably recall what the button is for
edge_cases.trigger: repeated teach-back attempts fail during training
edge_cases.mitigation: make no capacity or cognitive judgment; record that teach-back was not achieved, configure the account for caregiver-dependent use, tell the family plainly that button use cannot be relied upon here, and refer the care question to their clinician or care manager

edge_cases.description: The test signal arrives but the operator reads back a previous subscriber's address still attached to the reused device or account number
edge_cases.trigger: a refurbished device or recycled account number carries stale record data
edge_cases.mitigation: fail the test on the read-back, have the centre correct the record while the technician is still on site, and repeat the entire sequence from the first press rather than re-checking only the address

edge_cases.description: During a guided remote setup the relative holding the phone presses the button and speaks to the operator instead of the wearer
edge_cases.trigger: a family member substitutes for the wearer during the remote test or teach-back
edge_cases.mitigation: require the wearer's own press and the wearer's own voice on the two-way leg, re-run the affected legs, and record the teach-back in the wearer's words or mark it unachieved

workflow.action: Confirm the install scope and the go-live conditions before travelling
workflow.description: Load the visit with the definition of a completed install, the stop rules, and what arrives from the sales side: the disclosed offer, the device class provisionally chosen and the household's stated situation
workflow.artifact: visit brief carrying the go-live condition list and the stop rules
workflow.gate: the technician can state, before entering, every condition that would end the visit without the account going live

workflow.action: Re-establish the wearer's assent at the door
workflow.description: Tell the wearer plainly what will be attached to their home and body, what the centre will hear and when, what any location or caregiver-app sharing reveals and to whom, and confirm they choose to proceed
workflow.artifact: assent record including the sharing disclosure and the wearer's choices
workflow.gate: the wearer was told what is shared and with whom, chose to proceed, and knows they may stop the visit at any point

workflow.action: Walk and map the whole dwelling with the wearer
workflow.description: Record construction, levels, the rooms used at night, the bathroom and shower positions, the outdoor extent actually used, and the household constraints that bound the work
workflow.artifact: marked floor plan with usage geography and constraints
workflow.gate: all levels, the night route, the outdoor extent and every tenancy or household constraint are recorded, and any room the wearer declined to show is marked unsurveyed

workflow.action: Measure and choose the outbound signal path
workflow.description: Read served signal at the base position, the bed and the bathroom, establish whether any landline is really broadband-delivered, and identify which failure points the candidate paths share with the router and the mains
workflow.artifact: signal and line-type readings with the chosen path and its single points of failure
workflow.gate: the path is chosen from readings taken where the wearer sleeps and bathes, not at the front window, and shared failure points are named

workflow.action: Walk-test the pendant against the map
workflow.description: Trigger from each surveyed location with the pendant worn as it will be worn, recording pass, marginal or fail per location and retesting from alternative base positions where results are marginal
workflow.artifact: dead-spot map with a per-location result
workflow.gate: every surveyed location has a worn-pendant result and every marginal location is either resolved by relocation or written up as a disclosed limit

workflow.action: Fit the person and select the device class
workflow.description: Demonstrate the press with the proposed button, settle wearing style, water exposure and charging realism, then choose the class from the measured coverage and the sustainable habit and name the routine it will not cover
workflow.artifact: selection record citing the specific findings, with the uncovered routine in writing
workflow.gate: the wearer physically pressed the proposed button, chose the wearing style, and the uncovered part of their routine is stated and acknowledged

workflow.action: Place, mount and power the hardware, then retest
workflow.description: Site the base for coverage and voice reach on an unswitched outlet, mount supplementary buttons at fall-concentration points within the tenancy constraint, pull the plug to observe outage behaviour, and re-run the range test from the final position
workflow.artifact: placement record with fixing method, outlet choice and the post-placement retest results
workflow.gate: the retest passes at the critical locations, voice is audible from the bathroom floor position, and the outlet is confirmed unswitched and not on an extension lead

workflow.action: Provision the device and build the monitoring account
workflow.description: Register serials, activate the radio, apply pending firmware, pair every button, then write the dispatcher-facing record: verified dispatch address, wearer name and language, hearing note, entry method, with billing identity kept separate
workflow.artifact: account record plus a supervision check-in under the correct account number
workflow.gate: the dispatch address is verified against the premises rather than the contract, and the device checks in under its own account with all buttons paired

workflow.action: Verify the contact tree and configure the response instructions
workflow.description: Dial each proposed contact, obtain their consent and availability window, order by real reachability and keyholder status, then agree the per-account modifications to the centre's default sequence and confirm each is supportable
workflow.artifact: verified contact tree with consent evidence, plus a confirmed instruction set and a written statement of what the centre will not do
workflow.gate: every saved contact was reached and agreed, ordering is justified by reachability rather than rank, and each special instruction is confirmed by the centre

workflow.action: Run the end-to-end signal test in one uninterrupted sequence
workflow.description: Press from the bathroom floor position, hold a floor-level two-way conversation, take the operator's read-back of address, name, entry method and first contact, trigger each supplementary button, run the off-premise leg for a mobile unit, and complete the manufacturer's fall-detection check
workflow.artifact: test log with locations, timestamps, read-back confirmations and any failed attempt with its fix
workflow.gate: the full sequence passed without interruption after the last fix, and the signals are flagged and logged as tests

workflow.action: Train the wearer to teach-back and brief the family
workflow.description: Have the wearer press, speak to the operator, cancel a false alarm and state when they would press in their own words; then brief the family on what the service is and is not, their position in the contact tree, how to report changes and how cancellation works
workflow.artifact: teach-back record, large-print household card and caregiver acknowledgement
workflow.gate: the wearer demonstrated the press, the cancel and the when-to-press criteria unaided, and the family acknowledged the not-supervision statement and the change-reporting route

workflow.action: Decide go-live or not-live at the gate and close the record
workflow.description: Walk the binary condition list against the artifacts, complete the documentation packet, hand the account to the monitoring side, or leave it not live with the failed condition, the household's notification and a return date
workflow.artifact: completed gate checklist and handoff package, or a not-live record with the open item and return date
workflow.gate: every condition maps to an artifact in the record, or the account is explicitly not live and the household has been told so in writing

dominance_rules.rule: Wearer assent dominates payer authority at the installation
dominance_rules.rationale: the device is attached to a person's home and body and only works if that person wears and presses it; the fact that someone else paid does not transfer that decision
dominance_rules.trigger: the wearer objects to the install, the wearing style, a placement, or the whole arrangement
dominance_rules.action: stop, record the refusal or objection in the wearer's own words, do not activate the account, and return the commercial question to the sales side

dominance_rules.rule: A failed end-to-end test dominates every commercial and scheduling consideration
dominance_rules.rationale: an account that has not signalled successfully from a hard location is a promise of help that has never been demonstrated
dominance_rules.trigger: any leg of the test fails, including a marginal voice result or an incorrect read-back
dominance_rules.action: fix the named fault and repeat the entire sequence from the first press; if it cannot pass, leave the account not live with the failure recorded

dominance_rules.rule: Measured conditions dominate the configuration that was sold
dominance_rules.rationale: a specification sheet describes open air and an average building, while the measurement describes this dwelling and this wearer
dominance_rules.trigger: a reading or walk test contradicts the device class, tier or placement already agreed commercially
dominance_rules.action: redesign to what the measurements support or decline the install, reopen the commercial question with the household, and never adjust the record to match the invoice

dominance_rules.rule: The non-clinical boundary dominates the urge to be helpful
dominance_rules.rationale: clinical opinions given in a living room carry harm the operator cannot detect and liability it cannot carry
dominance_rules.trigger: a family or wearer asks for a judgment about falls, medication, capacity, driving or whether the person can live alone
dominance_rules.action: answer the equipment question fully, refer the clinical question to the physician, discharge planner or care manager, and log the question and the referral

dominance_rules.rule: The address verified at the premises dominates the address on the contract
dominance_rules.rationale: responders drive to the dispatch record, and the contract frequently carries the paying adult child's address
dominance_rules.trigger: the contract, billing and premises addresses disagree in any particular, including a missing unit number or entry lane
dominance_rules.action: set the dispatch record from what is verified on site, record the discrepancy, and confirm it in the operator read-back before accepting the test

dominance_rules.rule: Coverage-critical placement dominates appearance, and within the passing options the wearer's preference dominates
dominance_rules.rationale: a position that fails the retest cannot help anyone, but a position the household hates gets moved or unplugged the week after the visit
dominance_rules.trigger: the household objects to a base position, a wall button or a wearing style on grounds of appearance or convenience
dominance_rules.action: offer every alternative that passes the post-placement retest and let the wearer choose; if the household insists on a failing position, record it as a disclosed coverage compromise and do not waive the gate condition

dominance_rules.rule: Button training dominates reliance on automatic fall detection
dominance_rules.rationale: the sensor is an inference and the press is a decision; a household that treats the sensor as primary has bought a system that may never alert
dominance_rules.trigger: a wearer or family member describes the device as calling for help automatically if there is a fall
dominance_rules.action: restate and record the supplement-not-substitute sentence, re-run the press training, and capture the acknowledgement in the record

dominance_rules.rule: A consented and reachable contact dominates a senior but unreachable one
dominance_rules.rationale: the tree exists to produce a human at the door, and rank does not answer the phone at three in the morning
dominance_rules.trigger: the family orders the tree by seniority or lists someone unavailable, unwilling or far away at the top
dominance_rules.action: order by verified reachability, proximity and keyholder status, record the family's stated preference separately, and never save a contact who has not agreed

dominance_rules.rule: Remote installs receive no test waivers
dominance_rules.rationale: the household's risk does not decrease because the technician stayed in the office
dominance_rules.trigger: a mandatory verification element cannot be executed over a guided call
dominance_rules.action: record the item as unverified with a scheduled re-test, and where it is a go-live condition, dispatch a site visit or arrange the equipment's return rather than going live

dominance_rules.rule: The operator's data-handling rule dominates convenience for keys, codes and personal facts
dominance_rules.rationale: lockbox codes, gate codes and household details are exactly the data that turns a helpful service into a burglary risk
dominance_rules.trigger: an entry code, key location or personal detail needs to be captured or shared during the visit
dominance_rules.action: store it only in the monitoring account under the stated rule, never in a personal phone, a paper note left in the home or an unsecured message

anti_rework_rules.rule: Measure the outbound signal path and walk-test the pendant before unboxing, mounting or provisioning anything
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a full install, account build and training session performed on a device class the building cannot carry, which then has to be removed and redone

anti_rework_rules.rule: Survey the entire dwelling, including the night route and the outdoor extent, before selecting the device class
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a second visit and a second device when the shared basement laundry or the daily garden trip surfaces after the system is already installed

anti_rework_rules.rule: Choose and verify the outlet before fixing the base in place
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-siting the base after discovering the socket is on a wall switch, and the full range retest that relocation forces

anti_rework_rules.rule: Verify the dispatch address against the premises before running the end-to-end test
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a passed test recorded against a wrong record, and the correct-and-retest cycle that follows once the error surfaces

anti_rework_rules.rule: Dial and obtain consent from every contact before the tree is saved and the protocol configured
anti_rework_rules.prevents: rebuilding the tree and reconfiguring instructions after a dead number or an unwilling contact is discovered during a real event

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm each special instruction with the monitoring centre before describing it to the family
anti_rework_rules.prevents: promising behaviour the platform cannot hold, then re-briefing the household and rewriting the record after the centre declines it

anti_rework_rules.rule: Apply any pending firmware update before the test rather than after
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a validated configuration silently invalidated by an update that changes button, sensor or supervision behaviour

anti_rework_rules.rule: Re-run the range test from the final base position, never from the trial position
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a coverage map that describes a location the base no longer occupies, and the incident review that discovers it

anti_rework_rules.rule: Rehearse the false-alarm cancel with the wearer during the visit
anti_rework_rules.prevents: the abandonment spiral after the first embarrassing false alert, and the recovery visit and retraining it takes to undo

anti_rework_rules.rule: Write the coverage limits found in this home onto the household card before leaving
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a dispute months later about what was promised, and the re-verification work needed to reconstruct what was actually true at install

iteration_protocol.trigger: any leg of the end-to-end test fails, including a marginal two-way voice result or an incorrect operator read-back
iteration_protocol.action: fix the named fault, then repeat the entire sequence from the first press rather than resuming, and keep the failed attempt and its fix in the record

iteration_protocol.trigger: a marginal or failed pendant result at a location the wearer actually uses
iteration_protocol.action: relocate the base and re-walk the full map; if it stays marginal, disclose the limit in writing, reconsider the device class, and update the household card

iteration_protocol.trigger: the wearer cannot complete teach-back after repeated attempts
iteration_protocol.action: change the form factor or the teaching method and retrain; if still unachieved, record it plainly, reconfigure the account for caregiver-dependent use, and tell the family that button use cannot be relied on here

iteration_protocol.trigger: a proposed contact cannot be reached during the visit or declines to be listed
iteration_protocol.action: re-order the tree, recruit a local keyholder or neighbour with consent, and re-confirm the response instructions against the new order before the test

iteration_protocol.trigger: repeated false fall alerts or a report that a real fall produced no alert
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the manufacturer's prescribed check, rehearse the cancel window again, adjust only within supported settings, and restate the supplement-not-substitute framing to the household

iteration_protocol.trigger: a guided remote install's scheduled follow-up re-test finds a fault or an unverified item turns out to be wrong
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the full remote protocol or dispatch a site visit, and update the unverified-item list and the household card with what is now known

iteration_protocol.trigger: the household changes address, entry code, contacts, phone service or carrier after go-live
iteration_protocol.action: hand the change to the monitoring side and re-run the affected measurements and the end-to-end test before the record is treated as current again

iteration_protocol.trigger: a firmware, hardware or carrier network change alters behaviour that was previously measured
iteration_protocol.action: re-verify the affected measurements in the affected homes, relabel any claim that no longer traces to a current test, and update the recorded limits

iteration_protocol.trigger: the monitoring side reports incoming accounts with missing, stale or unusable fields
iteration_protocol.action: amend the gate condition list and the documentation template, retrain the installers on the specific field that failed, and re-check recently handed-over accounts

priority_rationale: The frame nodes come first because scope, the non-clinical line, the measure-before-claim rule and wearer assent govern what may be done in the home at all; assessment precedes selection because the dwelling's radio, power and human facts decide which device class is honest; placement, account construction, contact verification and response configuration follow selection because each is built on the class and the measurements; and verification, training, documentation and the binary go-live gate come last because they are what convert a configured system into a demonstrated one that can be handed to the monitoring side.
